thread.title: What's In My Portfolio: June 2018 Review

author: AllStarTrader
title: What's In My Portfolio: June 2018 Review
text:
My Portfolio Currently I figured I would offer a brief overview of what is in my portfolio for the followers who are interested. Everyone has their own investment objectives and should try to build a portfolio that meets what they are looking for short or long term.
Company (Ticker) % Of Portfolio Johnson & Johnson ( JNJ ) 8.58% AT&T ( T ) 8.57% FedEx ( FDX ) 8.34% Kimco ( KIM ) 7.81% Visa ( V ) 7.81% JD.com ( JD ) 7.25% Apple ( AAPL ) 6.38% Bank of America ( BAC ) 6.27% Facebook ( FB ) 5.92% Prudential ( PRU ) 5.83% Jernigan Capital ( JCAP ) 4.99% AbbVie ( ABBV )

PepsiCo ( PEP ) 4.67% STORE Capital ( STOR ) 3.96% Realty Income ( O ) 3.72% BlackRock Multi-Sector Income Trust ( BIT ) 2.99% Algonquin Power & Utilities Corp. ( AQN ) 2.34% Cash 0.5% These positions stay steady for the most part; however, their value changes with price fluctuations, of course. This month alone, I have added to my AT&T position, Realty Income Position, and started a position in AbbVie. I reduced shares of STORE Capital.
My Strategy Personally, I like investing in companies whose business I can understand or I am familiar with. I do have a closed-end fund in the portfolio, BIT, as it pays a dividend monthly. I did own this once before, sell it, and repurchase it as I had a gain and decided to deploy the funds into other trades at the time. This time, I decided to keep it as a monthly income generator and let the dividends reinvest. For now it is small, but as I let it DRIP, I plan on having it grow to approximately 5% of the portfolio. As for the rest, I believe in investing in the companies at a reasonable valuation and when levels are not at their highs.
I often believe that when sentiment is so negative that everyone is sour on the stock, it is the best time to invest, as any positive or unexpected news will most likely drive the stock higher. This year I was able to purchase FDX, AAPL, FB, O, and PEP at levels far below which they currently trade due to this.
I also believed in being paid for my investment. Just like a private company, when you make an investment, you are looking for a share of the profits. That is why most of the companies in my portfolio are dividend-paying stocks. While I do not need the income, I believe at my age (24) the dividend income stream is a great way to let compounding do its magic. The only non-dividend paying companies are JD and FB. Due to their growth profiles, I am okay with no dividend at this time.
I tend to keep all positions under 10%. I will only go over should there be a significant discount to fair or historical value, or should the value climb and I am not ready to sell.
While I typically prefer more cash on hand, I keep cash outside of the portfolio, ready to transfer should an opportunity to arise. So, for this reason, the cash % in the portfolio is often irrelevant.
Why Each One Has Its Place 1. JNJ - Long-standing Dividend Aristocrat, recession-resistant, large portfolio of products, and a long-term outperformer.
2. AT&T - Huge dividend and reliable growth in dividend for 33 years. Super-low P/E and cheap on every basis historically. The newly acquired Time Warner Media should help growth for years to come and create new service and product platforms for the company to offer.
3. FedEx - Successful growth domestically and abroad, huge dividend growth, cheap valuation at 15X earnings. Should continue to benefit from low competition and high eCommerce growth.
4. Kimco - High dividend yield and transforming its portfolio to be online-resistant. Save the payout from FFO and the investment grade balance sheet, the company can continue to acquire or develop great assets. Trades at low P/FFO multiple and offers a discount to historical norms.
5. Visa - Long runway for growth with developing countries slowly adopting cashless payment systems. Even today, most of the world's transactions are still cash leaving plenty of room for Visa to gain market share.
6. JD.com - The multiple partnerships and expansion avenues it is making into foreign countries will provide lots of growth. The value of assets and logistics far outweighs market cap, growth is exceptional.
7. Apple - Consumer products giant with a large cash pile, buying back shares, trades at a discount to the market and has been growing its dividend. I view this as a safe play in the tech space due to its loyal consumer base and consumers' need for the latest technology.
8. Bank of America - Long-term holding, it is going to trade more like a utility, and the dividend raises over the next few years will be great. We should know more after this week's capital return announcement. Trades at 10x earnings and is going to benefit from rising rates.
9. Facebook - Digital ad monster, still experiencing great growth, no debt, large cash pile, and still being innovative. The only place for businesses to reach consumers on such a scale and split ad dollars between not just one social platform but two at the same time. Should continue to earn more revenue, as it launched IGTV recently.
10. Prudential - Great yield, trades at 7x earnings, and should benefit from rising rates.
11. Jernigan Capital - Interesting play on the self-storage sector. Offers an outsized yield, secured with plenty of earnings leaving its payout at around 50%. Trades for 6x earnings, and its leader has a proven record of success in the industry. Valuation should expand as the company proves its model of financing and developing self-storage sites.
12. AbbVie - Great yield, the recent pullback allows for opportunity to benefit. I believe it has a great pharma pipeline and should see large revenue growth once these drugs come to market. Trades at a cheap forward multiple of 12x earnings.
13. PepsiCo - Historically high yield, it is becoming a play on healthy snacks and beverages as well as expanding its legacy soda and chip business. Should see growth from small acquisitions being leveraged via its sales network. The business is recession-resistant.
14. STORE Capital - Strong triple net lease REIT, offers stable yield, and has a strong eCommerce-resistant portfolio. At the time of purchase, shares were $21 and offered a compelling yield. I started to trim the position to invest funds in other companies with better valuations at this time. I would look to add the stock back should it have a 5% yield once again.
15. Realty Income - It is a recent addition to my REIT holdings and has a strong track record of growing dividends and paying monthly. I like the idea of the dividends compounding monthly, and the company has a strong portfolio and a great balance sheet. I look to add more when its yield is over 5%.
16. BlackRock Multi-Sector Income Trust - Monthly dividend CEF, trades at 8% discount to NAV. If I can get paid 8% while waiting for the fund to match its value in actual assets, why not? So, I continue to drip this one.
17. Algonquin Power & Utilities Corp. - Small utility, great growth, has been acquiring assets in the U.S., and has stated plans to grow its dividend 10% or more for the next few years. There aren't many utilities growing as fast as this company, and for that reason, I am interested in it. I will continue to add shares when I see fit or have funds available.
Currently, I have kept the weightings in the stocks rather steady. However, I look to grow the bottom-weighted ones and reduce the top-weighted ones when price targets are reached or return goals are met. I believe for now this works best for me and my age profile. While growth should certainly be a larger percentage of the portfolio, I personally prefer income and the effects of compounding.
Review Since I do most of the analysis in a security before I make my investment decision, I would like to share some of that here with you. I have recently reviewed AT&T here and FedEx here . An article on PEP should be available soon as well. I do wish to continue to add to some of my positions, such as PEP, ABBV, AQN, and O, however, I will wait until further opportunity present itself. If there is continuous trade war talk, I might just get that opportunity.
The hardest part of my investing strategy is learning when to let go. I am mixed between buying and holding and reducing a holding to take profit when necessary. Some holdings such as BAC, V, JNJ, and T have already been in the portfolio for many years, and I have no intention of selling them, as I believe in them for the long haul.
Let me know your thoughts on the portfolio as it stands today. If there is a certain entity you would like my review on first, let me know and I will try to offer my opinion as I can. I like not only reviewing my holdings, but those I believe to be over- or undervalued. Thank you for the time to review my portfolio, and stay tuned for more!
